study_identification_part.si_4_title: Linking Personalized Brain Atrophy to Schizophrenia Network and Treatment Response

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Data from a single site: University of Science and Technology of China (Hefei, China). 797 healthy adults used for structural MRI normative modeling, with 652 of them also having resting-state fMRI data for functional connectivity analysis. 91 schizophrenia patients from Anhui Mental Health Center were used for clinical application.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Structural and fMRI data were obtained at the University of Science and Technology of China (Hefei, China) with a 3-T scanner (Discovery 750; GE Healthcare, Milwaukee, WI, USA)." ... "This study included 797 healthy adults (18 to 45 years old, 411 females) and 91 schizophrenia patients." ... "Additionally, resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data were acquired for 652 of the 797 healthy subjects."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Ji2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Participants, L36-38; MRI Data and Preprocessing, L47-49

answer.SINGLE-SITE: normative modeling (n=797 HC for cortical thickness normative model; n=652 HC for functional connectivity/atrophy network mapping)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: 797 healthy controls were used to establish vertex-wise normative reference ranges for cortical thickness as a function of age and sex. 652 healthy subjects with rs-fMRI data were used to compute atrophy networks via seed-to-whole brain functional connectivity mapping.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The healthy subjects were used to establish normative reference ranges for cortical thickness as a function of age and sex." ... "Each patient's atrophy network was mapped using resting-state functional connectivity MRI from a subgroup of healthy subjects (n = 652)."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The normative model for cortical thickness was constructed using all 797 healthy controls. The study does not mention a separate train/validation/test split for the normative model construction. An independent validation group of 60 healthy subjects was used to validate the model predictions, but these were not part of the normative model itself.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We constructed a normative model by using the demographic and structural MRI data of 797 healthy individuals." ... "we additionally collected structural MRI data of an independent healthy group (n = 60, mean age ± SD = 25.3 ± 7.40, 34 women) ... These 2 validation groups were used to validate the normative model."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Ji2023.pdf.md: Results / Heterogeneous Structural Atrophy Loci, L97-99

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper only reports the age range (18-45 years) for the 797 healthy controls used in normative modeling. Mean and SD are not reported for the healthy control group. The independent validation healthy group (n=60) had mean age ± SD = 25.3 ± 7.40, but this group was not used for normative model training.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "This study included 797 healthy adults (18 to 45 years old, 411 females) and 91 schizophrenia patients."
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Ji2023.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Participants, L36-37

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: 797 healthy adults included 411 females (51.6%) and 386 males (48.4%, calculated as 797-411=386). Since no train/test split is reported, all 797 subjects are considered as the overall phase for normative model construction.
